principles.statement: Explore to generate hypotheses, not to confirm them — the first pass should widen the field, not narrow it.
principles.rationale: An exploration that goes looking for one thing finds only that thing and misses the pattern three columns over.

principles.statement: Change one lens at a time: distribution, then time, then groups, then relationships.
principles.rationale: Structured lenses keep exploration comparable across runs; random slicing produces anecdotes.

principles.statement: Record what you looked at and what it showed — negative results bound the search space too.
principles.rationale: Unrecorded exploration gets re-run by the next person (or you) with nothing to build on.

heuristics.name: Shape before outliers
heuristics.description: Look at the whole distribution (histogram/counts) before hunting extremes — outliers only mean something against the shape.
examples: A single 1e9 spike means clipping; a long tail means log-scale.

heuristics.name: Follow the surprise
heuristics.description: When something contradicts expectation, stop and pull that thread — it is either a data error or the most valuable finding of the pass.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any result that contradicts an assumption.
examples: Two groups with identical means but wildly different spreads is the finding.

decision_rules.condition: An exploratory finding will be relied on downstream.
decision_rules.action: Re-derive it deliberately: same data, scripted, reproducible — then it graduates from exploration to analysis.

decision_rules.condition: Exploration time exceeds the budget without a new hypothesis.
decision_rules.action: Stop and write down what was eliminated — knowing where the answer ISN'T is the deliverable.
